title: Energy-Flow Cosmology: Field Equations for Entropy-Driven Spacetime
description: Proposes a covariant field-theoretic framework where a normalized entropy field S(x) and an energy-flow four-vector J^μ source spacetime curvature alongside the metric. The action yields modified Einstein equations that reduce to GR when entropy gradients vanish, with cosmological and galactic-scale phenomenology that can mimic dark matter and alter late-time expansion.

action.description: Covariant action coupling the metric g_{\mu\nu} to an entropy potential S and an energy-flow four-vector J^\mu, with a Lagrange multiplier enforcing non-negative entropy production.

potential.description: Simple entropic potential that yields a cosmological constant term in the homogeneous (equilibrium) limit.

einstein_like.description: Einstein equations sourced by standard matter plus effective stress-energy from the entropy and energy-flow fields.

stress_energy_SJ.description: Effective stress-energy tensor arising from gradients of S, the flow J^\mu, and their coupling.

s_eom.description: Equation of motion for the entropy field S sourced by the divergence of the flow J^\mu.

j_eom.description: Constitutive relation connecting the energy-flow current J^\mu to gradients of S and the Lagrange multiplier.

entropy_production.description: Entropy production constraint consistent with the second law of thermodynamics.

rho_eff_newtonian.description: Effective energy density in the weak-field limit that modifies gravitational potentials and can mimic dark matter effects.

friedmann_bg.description: Modified Friedmann equations for a flat FRW background with homogeneous S(t) and J^0(t).

rho_p_SJ.description: Background effective energy density and pressure contributed by S and J^0 in cosmology.

key_results.main_finding: Introduces a covariant entropy–flow sector that sources curvature, recovers GR when ∇S → 0, and yields testable modifications to galactic dynamics, lensing, and the expansion history without invoking particle dark matter or dark energy.

sealed_predictions.statement: In galaxies, a single parameter set (kappa_S, kappa_J, gamma, V(S)) that fits rotation curves using baryons only will predict the corresponding weak-lensing convergence profile via ρ_eff^{S,J} without additional dark matter.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Joint kinematics–lensing samples (e.g., SPARC + KiDS/DES/LSST) showing inconsistent lensing-kinematics predictions across radii at >5σ for any parameter set satisfying Solar-System bounds.

sealed_predictions.statement: A homogeneous S(t) and J^0(t) background can fit Planck CMB, BAO, and SNe expansion data without Λ and CDM by adjusting {kappa_S, kappa_J, gamma, V(S)}.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Global fit to Planck TTTEEE+lensing + BAO + SNe showing Δχ² ≥ 50 degradation versus ΛCDM for all stable (no-ghost, no-gradient-instability) parameter choices.

sealed_predictions.statement: Solar-system PPN parameters reduce to GR values in regions with negligible ∇S and J^μ, implying |γ_PPN−1|, |β_PPN−1| ≲ 10⁻⁵.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Shapiro-delay, light-deflection, and perihelion-precession measurements improving or matching Cassini bounds but detecting deviations inconsistent with any allowed small-gradient EFC limit.

kill_criteria: KC1: No GR limit — if Solar-System PPN bounds (e.g., |γ_PPN−1| < 2.3×10⁻⁵) cannot be satisfied simultaneously with any cosmologically viable {kappa_S, kappa_J, gamma, V(S)}.
KC2: Global cosmology failure — if Planck TTTEEE+lensing + BAO + SNe fits require Δχ² ≥ 50 worse than ΛCDM across the full stable EFC parameter space.

KC3: Instabilities — if linear perturbation analysis shows ghosts (negative kinetic terms) or gradient instabilities (c_s^2 < 0) in the late Universe for parameter regions needed to match background expansion or structure growth.
KC4: Second-law violation — if fitting observations necessitates negative entropy production (Σ < 0) over sustained cosmological epochs.
KC5: Scale inconsistency — if parameters that fit the FRW background and CMB cannot reproduce galaxy/cluster lensing–dynamics relations without dark matter across multiple systems.

KC6: Early-Universe constraints — if Big Bang Nucleosynthesis or CMB damping-tail inferences of H(t) imply ΔN_eff or expansion rates incompatible with EFC modifications at >3σ when using the same parameter set.
